paragraphs.source_en: Despite, or perhaps because of, all his successes on military and diplomatic fronts, Ibrahim Pasha was suddenly executed on Suleiman I’s orders during the Ides of March in 1536. After no hint that he was no longer the sultan’s favourite, Ibrahim was strangled in his sleep in his bedroom in the harem of Topkapi Palace after having earlier broken the Ramadan fast with Suleiman I. The man who had been the sultan’s ‘breath and heart’ was buried in an obscure grave.” The sultan could promote his inexperienced converted male favourite whom he passionately loved to the highest office in government, bestow upon him an extraordinary income and a magnificent palace to go with it, and even pay for his wedding. He could also murder this slave arbitrarily and without trial to show who was master.
